cells.tense: Right now you are carrying a spark into a room and trusting it to land.
cells.act: cut to the logic and act on it
cells.ask: When a conversation starts circling, name the point that matters, plainly, and stop talking there.
cells.core:
At a table where you and another person are level, you can bring heat without performing it. That's the whole of what's working: your enthusiasm is real, so people lean in, and you aren't asking them to hold it for you. Both of you stay honest about what's here, and that honesty is the connection.

Sharpen it. When something matters in a conversation, most people circle it. Get to the middle — state the actual point, skip the throat-clearing — and watch what the honesty does between you. You don't have to soften it into a question or pad it afterward. Your fire gets useful the moment you stop warming the air and say the thing instead.
cells.sheetLine: You bring real heat, and you trust it to land.
cells.verb: lighting the fire and finding out where it wants to go
cells.place: at the table where you and another person are actually level

cells.tense: You are already rehearsing how the next conversation will go before anyone has said anything.
cells.act: perceive it with fresh eyes before judging
cells.ask: Let a beat pass before you answer someone this week, and answer what they actually said rather than the shape you expected.
cells.core:
You've started arriving early in your own head when you sit down with someone. You can feel the connection coming before it gets here, so you sketch your half in advance; the other person walks into a script they didn't agree to. The warmth that brought people in is now steering them toward a version of themselves you already drew.

Try the other direction. When someone starts talking, wait a beat before answering, and take in what they did say — the particular words, the particular mood — instead of the familiar shape you were braced for. Curiosity is the correction here. You don't have to know where the conversation lands. You can find out at the same pace they do.

cells.tense: You used to step toward people with your whole chest and now you hold back at the door.
cells.act: tend the small thing and learn from it
cells.ask: Put your hands on one small living thing this week — a pot by the window, a herb — and give it a few days of what it asks for.
cells.core:
You've gone quiet when you're level with someone. The aliveness that used to make you reach toward people first is set down, and you're standing still while the room moves. What your warmth runs on has gone dry, and pushing feeling at it won't refill it.

Instead of working on the connection directly, put your hands on something alive and small. Basil on a sill. A plant you've walked past. Water it for a few days and pay attention to what it wants — light, less water, more room. Care for a thing that is quietly telling you what it needs. This isn't rehearsal for the people in your life. It's the refill, and it comes back through your hands.
cells.sheetLine: You've stopped stepping toward people. Tend something small first.
cells.verb: lighting the fire and finding out where it wants to go
cells.place: at the table where you and another person are actually level

cells.tense: Warmth is moving through you toward people, and you are calling it nothing much.
cells.act: lay the one step you can see, solidly
cells.ask: Think of one person you've held steady for, and note the specific thing you did — the call, the ride, the remembering. Keep it as yours.
cells.core:
You already reach toward people — remembering the worry they mentioned, checking in, holding a seat for them — and you describe it as just how you are, as nothing worth naming. Where you and another are level, you're doing the load-bearing and filing it under luck. That isn't modesty. It's someone else's name on work of yours.

Take one concrete move you made for someone and look at it plainly. Don't dismiss it as circumstance or as small. You don't have to announce it or argue for it; simply let yourself see the move as one you made. That's how what you do comes back under your own name — and once it's yours, you can build on it instead of handing it off to chance.
cells.sheetLine: You hold people steady and file it under nothing.
